Almased ist eine der bekanntesten Marken im Bereich Ernährungs- und Gesundheitsprodukte im deutschsprachigen Raum. Seit Jahrzehnten steht die Marke für wissenschaftlich fundierte Ernährungskonzepte zur Optimierung des Stoffwechsels, sowie nachhaltige Gewichtsregulation.
Seit über 30 Jahren, gestartet am Küchentisch in Bienenbüttel, sind wir Marktführer in Deutschland – und auch in UK und den USA aktiv.

Geblieben sind wir ein kleines, engagiertes Team mit der großen Vision, Menschen durch Ernährung dabei zu unterstützen, ihre persönlichen Ziele zu erreichen.Zur Unterstützung unseres Teams sowie unserer HR- und Office-Prozesse suchen wir eine strukturierte, zuverlässige und proaktive Persönlichkeit in Teilzeit (20–30 Stunden/Woche), die Freude daran hat, Verantwortung zu übernehmen, mitzudenken und gemeinsam mit uns Strukturen weiterzuentwickeln.

Du arbeitest gerne eigenverantwortlich, hast Freude daran, anderen den Rücken freizuhalten und behältst auch dann den Überblick, wenn mehrere Themen gleichzeitig auf Dich zukommen?

If you do not provide evidence that you possess the following selective factor(s), you will be rated not qualified. Selective Factor: The duties of this position require the ability to type at least 40 words per minute based on a five-minute typing test with three or fewer mistakes.

Specialized experience is defined as demonstrated experience performing administrative functions such as payroll, personnel, travel, procurement, budget, and/or formal correspondence.

You must include hours per week worked. -OR- Education: Successful completion of at least four years of education above high school (120 semester hours or 180 quarter hours) in any field for which high school graduation or the equivalent is the normal prerequisite. You must include transcripts. -OR- Combination of education and experience.

To combine education and experience, only education is excess of the first 60 semester hours of a course of study leading to a bachelor's degree is creditable toward meeting the specialized experience requirements. Two full academic years of study, or 60 semester hours, beyond the second year is equivalent to 1 year of specialized experience.

Then take the number of months of full-time experience and divide by 12 months. Add the percentages together. The total must equal at least 100 percent to qualify. You must include hours per week and transcripts.

Specialized experience is defined as demonstrated experience performing a wide variety of advanced administrative functions such as coordinating payroll, prepared and entered personnel actions, coordinating travel arrangements, managing a procurement system, and preparing, tracking, and reconciling an organization's budget.

You must include hours per week worked. To qualify for this position at the GS-07 grade level: Experience: You must possess at least one full year of specialized experience equivalent to the GS-06 level in the Federal service (obtained in either the public or private sectors).

Specialized experience is defined as demonstrated experience performing a wide variety of advanced administrative functions such as advising employees on payroll regulations and serving as payroll coordinator; Serving as liaison with Human Resources by preparing and entering personnel actions, processing employee paperwork, and coordinating background investigations; Serving as the technical advisor for travel processes and regulations; Advising on procurement; Performing budget and financial management by collecting data for a budget, making recommendations, tracking expenditures, creating budgetary reports, and reconciling an organization's budget.

Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge, and skills and can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment. You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience.

Interagency Career Transition Assistance Plan (ICTAP): The ICTAP provides eligible displaced Federal competitive service employees with selection priority over other candidates for competitive service vacancies.

If your agency has notified you in writing that you are a displaced employee eligible for ICTAP consideration, you may receive selection priority if: 1) this vacancy is within your ICTAP eligibility; 2) you apply under the instructions in the announcement; and 3) you are found well-qualified for this vacancy.

To be well-qualified, you must satisfy all qualification requirements for the vacant position and receive a score of 85 or better on established ranking criteria. You must provide proof of eligibility to receive selection priority.

Such proof may include a copy of your written notification of ICTAP eligibility or a copy of your separation personnel action form.Additional information about ICTAP eligibility is at: http://www.opm.gov/policy-data-oversight/workforce-restructuring/employee-guide-to-career-transition/.

Career Transition Assistance Plan (CTAP): The CTAP provides eligible surplus and displaced competitive service employees in the Department of Justice with selection priority over other candidates for competitive service vacancies.

If your Department of Justice component has notified you in writing that you are a surplus or displaced employee eligible for CTAP consideration, you may receive selection priority if: 1) this vacancy is within your CTAP eligibility, 2) you apply under the instructions in this announcement, and 3) you are found well-qualified for this vacancy.

To be well qualified, you must satisfy all qualification requirements for the vacant position and receive a score of 85 or better on established ranking criteria. You must provide a copy of your written notification of CTAP eligibility with your application.

Additional information about CTAP eligibility is at http://www.opm.gov/policy-data-oversight/workforce-restructuring/employee-guide-to-career-transition/. You will monitor and oversee accession training procurement activities, ensuring requirements align with short- and long-term command actions.
You will draft acquisition plans, technical specifications, and Statements of Work (SOWs) for command hardware, software, and training systems.
You will lead post-award conferences, negotiate contract modifications, and manage procurement system accounts (Navy-ERP, WAWF, PD2).
You will coordinate Contracting Officer Representative (COR) functions across commands and independently resolve complex contracting disputes.
You will provide regulatory procurement advice to command leadership in coordination with legal counsel.
You will manage procurement strategies, policies, and tuition compliance for NROTC Educational Service Agreements (ESAs) with universities.
You will formulate long-range educational procurement plans and evaluate state and federal legal applicability.
You will train and evaluate domain CORs and Technical Assistants on contract compliance and oversight procedures.
You will investigate labor and performance issues, review claims, determine allowable costs, dispose of government property, and finalize contract closeouts.
You will lead hiring efforts, identify training opportunities, and resolve employee grievances under EEO guidelines.
In addition to the Basic Requirements for this position, your resume must also demonstrate at least one year of specialized experience at or equivalent to the GS-11 grade level or pay band in the Federal service or equivalent experience in the private or public sector.

Specialized experience must demonstrate the following: 1) Applying contract administration principles to manage and oversee complex contract types, such as fixed-price, cost-reimbursement, and incentive contracts, throughout the entire acquisition lifecycle; 2) Conducting price and cost analysis on proposals to establish negotiation positions, resolve invoice issues, and process modifications; 3) Managing contract terminations (convenience or default) by evaluating settlement proposals, resolving disputes, and executing closeouts; 4) Developing and implementing quality assurance surveillance plans (QASPs) and utilizing various oversight techniques to monitor and evaluate contractor performance against technical and administrative contract requirements; 5) Interpreting and applying federal and state laws impacting tuition policies and agreements to administer contracts and Educational Service Agreements (ESAs) with colleges and universities.

NOTE: All experience must be fully demonstrated in your resume to be considered for the position. This is a Defense Acquisition Workforce position that requires a Contracting, Foundational acquisition certification. The incumbent has 36 months to earn this certification.

Incumbent must obtain and maintain certification in accordance with DoD Instruction 5000.66. Acquisition Workforce (AWF) members must complete 80 hours of Continuous Learning Points (CLPs) every two (2) years, in accordance with DoDI 5000.66.

Workforce members are encouraged to earn their CLPs by completing Defense Acquisition University (DAU) Credentials. Obtaining certification within the allotted grace period and maintaining CLPs before and after achieving certification are conditions of employment.

Failure to meet these requirements could result in disciplinary action and/or removal from employment.

Applicant must meet the following Department of Defense qualification requirements for 1102 contracting positions: http://www.secnav.navy.mil/donhr/Documents/CivilianJobs/DoD_Qualification_Standard_For_GS-1102.pdf And the title 10 requirements found here: http://uscode.house.gov/view.xhtml?req=granuleid:USC-prelim-title10-section1724&num=0&edition=prelim Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., professional, philanthropic, religious, spiritual, community, student, social).

Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge, and skills and can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment.

The Administrative Officer position includes, but is not limited to, the following duties: Develops and advises on administrative requirements for a complex organization and actively participates in developing and implementing administrative management policies.

Analyzes organizational priorities and provides a wide range of liaison services to support administrative aspects for a significant agency component. Gathers data and analyzes information for serviced organizations. Analyzes impact of new programs in terms of costs and resources required to support varied levels of program operations.

Identifies problem areas, analyzes situations, recommends viable solutions and prepares reports as required. Analyzes and evaluates, on a quantitative or qualitative basis, the effectiveness of administrative programs or operations in meeting established goals and objectives.

Human Resources - Coordinates human resources actions and advises staff on IC, agency, and Federal human resources regulations, procedures and policies relative to Federal employees and contract personnel. Facilities Management - serves as the point of contact for problems and inquiries related to the space that employees occupy.

Property Management - manages distribution of accountable property, manages property contract, reconciles lost or missing accountable property, and tracks loaned property/issues property passes. Reviews requests for acquisition of surplus property.

Time and Attendance--Serves as point of contact for the timekeeping system and oversees other timekeepers in the proper use of the program, e.g. input of employee information.

Travel - Interprets policies, procedures, and practices concerning all aspects of travel, local, sponsored, domestic and/or foreign, and reimbursement for travel expenses for all orders and vouchers within the employee's assigned area(s).

Budget and Financial Management - plans, develops, formulates, prepares, executes, monitors, and/or forecasts organizational budgets.
You qualify at the GS-11 level, if you meet one of the following qualification requirements: Completed a Ph.D. or equivalent doctoral degree, or 3 full years of progressively higher level graduate education leading to such a degree or an LL.M., if related OR You must demonstrate in your resume at least one (1) year of qualifying experience equivalent to at least the GS-09 level in the Federal service obtained in either the private or public sector, performing the following types of tasks:1) Participating in the preparation and execution of organizational budgets. 2) Reconciling monthly expenditures against allocated funding. 3) Drafting specifications and statements of work for service contracts and equipment leases, including conducting negotiations with vendors. 4) Assisting in performing general administration and advisory services and/or functions, such as time and attendance, human resources services, facilities management, property management, and space/logistics, safety/security OR A combination of post baccalaureate education and experience that meets 100% of the qualification requirements for this position.

You qualify at the GS-12 level, if you meet the following qualification requirement: You must demonstrate in your resume at least one (1) year of qualifying experience equivalent to at least the GS-11 level in the Federal service obtained in either the private or public sector, performing the following types of tasks: 1) Preparing, executing and monitoring organizational budgets. 2) Analyzing and evaluating financial information to assess overall financial performance of an organization and making recommendations to improve performance. 3) Developing acquisition plans and cost estimates; monitoring contract performance and compliance with terms and conditions of purchase orders. 4) Verifying accurate distribution of accountable property and resolving property management discrepancies. 5) Providing advice on staffing and recruitment issues.

You qualify at the GS-13 level, if you meet the following qualification requirement: You must demonstrate in your resume at least one (1) year of qualifying experience equivalent to at least the GS-12 level in the Federal service obtained in either the private or public sector, performing the following types of tasks: 1) Planning, developing, executing and monitoring budgets with many different sources and types of funding. 2) Performing contract administration duties including planning and managing contract and equipment leases. 3) Serving as approving official for requisitions of equipment, supplies, and other materials and services. 4) Providing advice in a variety of human resource areas such as staffing and recruitment, employee development and training, and conflict resolution. 5) Developing standards/policies/procedures involving administrative functions in an organization.

You will receive credit for all experience material to the position, including experience gained in religious, civic, welfare, service, and organizational activities, regardless of whether you received pay.

Rigueur, esprit d'équipe et orientation solutions guident notre action au quotidien, au service d'une économie dynamique et innovante.
Le pôle Médias valorise les entreprises membres, gère les relations avec les médias et renforce l'influence de la FER auprès des décideurs, des médias et du grand public. Média de référence des entrepreneurs romands, Entreprise romande informe sur les enjeux économiques, politiques et entrepreneuriaux, met en lumière les membres de la FER et partage conseils pratiques et bonnes pratiques, au service d'une économie dynamique, innovante et créatrice de valeur.
Votre mission
Rattaché·e à la Directrice du Pôle Média, vous contribuez directement à ces missions au quotidien.
Au sein de l'équipe d'Entreprise romande, vous garantissez la fluidité opérationnelle du département, tout en participant progressivement à son développement commercial. Vous assurez :
Le secrétariat du département ;
La gestion et le développement des abonnés d'Entreprise romande ;
Le développement des annonceurs et des partenariats publicitaires ;
Le suivi comptable du département et de la publication.
Vous offrez ainsi à l'équipe une base administrative fiable et structurée, directement au service de la production éditoriale.
Responsabilités principales
1\. Gestion du secrétariat du département
Assurer la gestion usuelle du secrétariat : accueil téléphonique, courriers, agendas et organisation des réunions internes.
Apporter un appui administratif transversal aux membres de l'équipe d'Entreprise romande.
2\. Développement commercial et gestion des abonnés d'Entreprise romande
Tenir à jour le fichier des abonnés : créations, mutations et résiliations.
Participer à la prospection, la fidélisation et le développement du portefeuille d'abonnés.
Répondre aux demandes des abonnés et garantir un service client de qualité.
Contribuer au développement des annonceurs et des partenariats publicitaires, avec une montée en compétences progressive sur ce volet commercial.
3\. Comptabilité du département et d'Entreprise romande
Traiter les factures fournisseurs, suivre les paiements et préparer les pièces justificatives.
Collaborer avec le département comptabilité pour les clôtures et le reporting financier.
4\. Gestion documentaire et autres activités
Gestion documentaire : classer les articles d'Entreprise romande dans Syracuse, envoyer les justificatifs aux personnes concernées, archiver les contrats et les journaux.

Relecture : effectuer la relecture des textes et contenus du département.

Die meisten zählen Schafe um diese Zeit - Sie aber die Paletten.
Für die nationale LKW-Disposition suchen wir eine Sachbearbeiterin für die Nachtschicht. Sie behalten den Überblick über die laufenden Touren, stehen mit Chauffeuren in Kontakt und sorgen dafür, dass die Ware auch mitten in der Nacht dort ankommt, wo sie hingehört. Wenn irgendwo etwas nicht nach Plan läuft, sind Sie zur Stelle und finden eine Lösung.

· disponieren und koordinieren von nationalen LKW-Touren während der Nachtschicht
· überwachen der laufenden Transporte und Lieferungen
· koordinieren und betreuen der Chauffeure unterwegs
· reagieren auf Verspätungen, Ausfälle und kurzfristige Änderungen
· entgegennehmen und bearbeiten von Kunden- und Chauffeuranfragen
· erfassen und bearbeiten von Transportaufträgen und Lieferinformationen
· übergeben der wichtigsten Informationen an die Tagesschicht

kurzfristig oder nach Vereinbarung

Nachts ist die Dispo kleiner besetzt, dafür läuft vieles direkt über Sie. Sie wissen, welcher LKW wo unterwegs ist, welche Lieferung noch fehlt und welcher Chauffeur gerade Ihre Hilfe braucht. Wenn um zwei Uhr morgens etwas schiefläuft, gibt es keine zehn Personen, die zuerst gefragt werden müssen - Sie schauen, was zu tun ist, und machen es. Wenn Sie lieber Paletten als Schafe zählen und auch nachts einen kühlen Kopf behalten, könnte das ziemlich gut passen.
